Support and Guidance for Parents/Carers
We aim to work in partnership with our families, recognising that we are all here to support each other so that children can become the best person they can be. This page will provide links, resources and support for parents and carers to help them support their child.
Some of these resources are designed for children with a range of Special Educational Needs, but could be used by all parents. We have also added additional resources to help manage your child's emotional needs during this period of lockdown and links to family support networks.
We aim to add to this list on a regular basis, so please keep checking for new ideas.
If you have any further questions, or need to speak to us personally, please contact us by email or arrange a meeting via the School Office.

Governors
Governors work in partnership with the headteacher and other senior leaders to provide strategic leadership and promote and support the success of the school and to secure the best possible education for every child in the school.
The Governors are responsible for ensuring that the school has a broad and balanced curriculum, that it is safe and secure and that the ethos and environment helps children to learn and thrive. They are also responsible for monitoring the school's finances and work with the headteacher to make the tough decisions about balancing resources. As a Catholic school, Foundation Governors also ensure that the school continues to promote the mission of the Catholic church through the policies and practices.
The Governing Board is made up of:
7 Foundation Governors appointed by the Bishop
1 Local Authority Governor
2 Parent Governors elected by the Parent Community
and the Head teacher Governor
Individual Governors do not act independently; decisions are the joint responsibility of the governing body as they act as a corporate body.
Their key function is:
The Governing Body meets once per half term. In addition, each Governor sits on one or more committee and is responsible for an aspect of the work of the Governing body.

The online world rapidly develops and changes which can make it difficult for parents and children to stay up to date with the latest devices, platforms, apps, trends and the related threats. SEND and Inclusion
At Corpus Christi Catholic Primary School, we are committed to providing an excellent education for all our pupils where barriers to learning and participation are removed.
We promote a whole school approach to the delivery of SEND and Inclusion, underpinned by our Catholic values and fully inclusive ethos. All pupils, including those with special educational needs or a disability, will have provision, which enables them to achieve their best and develop secure social and emotional skills in order to become confident individuals and live fulfilling lives.
For more information, please look at our SEN Policy and Information Report.
Meet the Inclusion Lead
Our Inclusion Leader is Miss N. Fripp. Please do contact her is you have any concerns about your child.
We do hope that you find the SEND Information Report useful, however if there is something that you would like more information about then please leave a message with our school office or email us using the address below:
senco@corpuschristicp.school

Curriculum
Our Vision for the Curriculum
Corpus Christi will be a model of educational excellence. The school will achieve this through the delivery of a rich curriculum which inspires, motivates and challenges all of our children. Children will leave Corpus Christi confident in their abilities, polite, articulate and ambitious for their future growth at secondary school and beyond.
We will achieve our vision by living out our mission statement, “We live our lives like Jesus.”
The curriculum at Corpus Christi firmly underpins our vision and mission statement, from which a culture and ethos is generated that supports the spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of the whole school community.
Key to all learning at Corpus Christi is our belief that all children can achieve and find success; hence our rationale for learning is to provide opportunities for children to practice, consolidate and embed key knowledge and skills from across the curriculum, through recalling pre-knowledge, repetition, clear modelling and scaffolding and hands on-practical experiences, leading to the confidence to tackle new learning and key concepts that are embedded in long term memory.
